Wohnhaus an der Grünen Heide 18. Die Kar: The house at Grüne Heide 18. The map starts here. OpenStreetMap records the street as fine gravel. What happens in the house and on the street is something this map does not know.
An der Allertal 15, der Landesstraße dur: At Allertal 15, the main road through Ettenbüttel, stands a single-storey four-post hall house with brick infill and a half-hipped roof, the entrance in the middle of the long side. It is a listed building. This map does not say when it was built.
Hirtenwinkel 4 ist ebenfalls ein Vierstä: Hirtenwinkel 4 is another four-post hall house, brick infill under a half-hipped roof, with a stable wing set across it. It is listed.
In Bokelberge, nördlich von Ettenbüttel,: In Bokelberge, north of Ettenbüttel, stands a two-storey timber storehouse. The upper floor juts out on every side, under a gabled roof. It is listed.
Die Aller fließt nördlich an Ettenbüttel: The Aller flows past the north of Ettenbüttel. The Oker lies to the west. The two rivers meet in the main village of Müden, about five kilometres northwest of here and off this sheet.
Ettenbüttel ist ein Ortsteil von Müden (: Ettenbüttel is a part of Müden (Aller) in the district of Gifhorn, southeast of the main village. On 1 March 1974 it was incorporated into Müden together with Dieckhorst, Flettmar and Hahnenhorn. On 1 May 2024, 644 people lived here. In 1668 the Müden pastor Heinrich Hoffmann noted that the people of Ettenbüttel still paid the tithe, because the place had once belonged to the Müden parish. St. Petri, the church of the main village, stands about five kilometres northwest and is not on this sheet.
Die Karte öffnet am Wohnhaus Grüne Heide: The map opens at the house on Grüne Heide 18. This sheet holds Ettenbüttel, Grüne Heide and Bokelberge. The main village of Müden, with St. Petri, is about five kilometres northwest and off the sheet. What only the people here know is still missing: the festival, the bathing place, the names of the farms.
